acceptance_criteria.notes: reply-test green on interpreter and strict VM; async-test green (9 scenarios incl. prefetch, adopt, refund, missing worker, quit, real worker under stub, native PTY). prefetch-test folded into async-test (deviation documented in plan). Full validate and CI not yet evidenced (executor running validate; M4 open).

correctness_robustness.notes: Deferred commit matches the saved-words path (command/roll/seed depend only on policy, request, seed, label; verified by domain-record equality). Result files validated (schema, job id, calls 0..1, sizes); words read from the validated cache with the reserved roll, not from the result file. Workers stopped on quit and on every loop error path via Exit.running. Refund capped at callLimit. Prediction mirrors act/askProject (stage == commit's state; same ids, seed, signature). Main gap: cancelling a worker mid-generation leaves the dialogue cache lock dir behind, permanently blocking that signature.

test_quality.notes: Scenarios are well constructed (waitfor patterns only appear after the event; job-2 absence proves no re-dispatch; domain-record equality proves commit identity; PTY test proves idle redraw). Gaps: one tautological jq clause; 13 reply_jobs contracts never exercised (no generator, masked by --allow-skips); no test that an arrival leaves cursor/page/editor untouched; prefetch only tested in --legacy mode; no explicit out-of-order completion test.

docs_bookkeeping.notes: README/AGENT/CHANGELOG/help text accurate; sprint plan and JSON truthfully leave M4 open (status in_progress). CHANGELOG says eight scenarios, test has nine; design doc acceptance still names a prefetch-test target.

defects.summary: stop()/cancelProcess kills a worker on quit (incl. default prefetches) or on the 120 s timeout (line 55-57) while it may be inside store.locked (store.ail:146-155) holding ${home}/cache/<key>.lock. Nothing removes a stale lock, so every later resolve for that signature returns 'dialogue cache busy' forever (sessions included). Previously only a user Ctrl-C could do this; now the product does it routinely.
defects.verified_by: reading (store.ail has no stale-lock recovery; fixture worker sleeps before locking so async-test cannot see it)

defects.summary: If adapter.run returns Err (terminal scope failure) the Exit with running handles is lost and exit(1) leaves background workers orphaned (they may still make one AI call and write the cache).

Queued prefetches for an earlier state are never withdrawn when the state moves on; they are still dispatched later and spend allowance (down to the reserve of 3) on offers that can no longer be made with that signature.
Workers cancelled at quit get no wording record, so an attempted provider call in flight is not journalled (the timeout path does charge calls:1). Journal usage can under-report attempts.
defects.verified_by: reading (scenario 3 asserts zero wording records after quit)

defects.summary: readFileResult reads the whole result file before decodeOutcome's 8 KiB bound; the bound should be checked on file size first (low risk: trusted local worker, fs-max-bytes 16MB).
workerAvailable only tests fileExists on PATH entries, not executability; a non-executable crew-reply-worker would still reach spawnProcess, which aborts the run on failure (ailang#1784).
Replies view is newest-first, so an arrival while reading Replies prepends text and shifts the current page's content (page index unchanged, content moves).
Clause `$w[0].seed==$w[0].seed` is a tautology; it asserts nothing (presumably meant seed == 42 / the pending seed).

reply-test uses --allow-skips; output shows '13 properties never ran (no generator)' for reply_jobs, so the claimed contracts (bounded live jobs, complete only changes Preparing, etc.) are not exercised; only 4 example tests cover them. No out-of-order completion test despite the plan's claim.

All async scenarios run --legacy (watch-v2); prefetch prediction exactness is not tested in the default conversation watch (watch-v3), and no test checks that an arrival leaves cursor/page/editor text unchanged (a README/CHANGELOG claim).
Says async-test has 'eight installed scenarios'; test-async.sh has nine (sprint plan says nine).

summary: Solid, well-scoped implementation: decisions commit immediately with byte-identical domain records, workers are file-protocol isolated with validated results, allowance reservation/refund is bounded, prefetch prediction mirrors the real offer path and is proven by test, and quit/error paths stop workers. Provider-free suites pass. One major robustness issue (killed workers can leave a permanent cache lock) and several minor gaps in tests and docs. PASS at 80, conditional on the executor's make validate and CI being green (M4 still open).
